items.text: b The crude oil (mixture of hydrocarbons) is heated until it boils. The vapour passes into a fractionating column. The temperature is higher at the bottom of the column than at the top. Different fractions condense and are drawn off at different heights in the column. The hydrocarbons with the highest boiling points (longer chains) condense towards the bottom of the column. The smaller hydrocarbon molecules travel further up the column until they condense and are drawn off.
